 Purdue University is expected to announce its next official president on Thursday at the recently announced special board of trustees meeting, sources say.
 Speculation exists that finalists for the job include at least one candidate from the private sector and at least one internal candidate.
 The board has been searching for a permanent president since former president Mung Chiang's departure to Northwestern earlier this summer. Sources say the goal was to finalize the next university president before Purdue's homecoming weekend, which kicks off Thursday night.
 The board of trustees announced Tuesday that there will be a special meeting at 3:30 p.m. Thursday in the Stewart Center, Room 326. This will be the third board of trustees meeting since Purdue Interim President Mitch Daniels took over on July 1. There is not yet an agenda, but one will be posted at the entrance prior to the meeting, which is open to the public and media.
